moments.title: Werckmeister's well-temperament
moments.body: Werckmeister publishes tuning systems allowing all 24 keys to be playable on keyboard instruments, with different keys retaining different character.
moments.takeaway: Tuning systems are choices about which intervals to compromise, not natural facts.

moments.title: The Well-Tempered Clavier book one
moments.body:
Bach completes a set of preludes and fugues in every major and minor key.

Scholarship suggests he assumed a well temperament, not modern equal temperament.
moments.takeaway: Western tonal music expanded into all 24 keys as tuning systems made them usable.

moments.title: International conference on pitch
moments.body:
Delegates recommend A=440 Hz as concert pitch standard.

ISO 16:1955 confirms it.
moments.takeaway: Concert pitch is a 20th-century international standard, not an ancient tradition.

now.title: Tuning today
now.body: Most fixed-pitch instruments use equal temperament. Historically informed performance recovers earlier temperaments; some electronic instruments support microtonal alternatives.
now.open_questions: What musical possibilities open up when digital instruments make microtuning trivially accessible?

items.reflection: Every tuning is a compromise. Which one a culture standardises on shapes which music sounds 'in tune'.

moments.title: Sonata form crystallises
moments.body: What 19th-century theorists will call 'sonata form' emerges as a flexible scheme of exposition, development and recapitulation across keyboard, chamber and orchestral works.
moments.takeaway: Forms studied in textbooks are often retroactive reconstructions.

moments.title: Beethoven's Ninth premiere
moments.body:
The Ninth Symphony introduces vocal soloists and chorus into the symphonic form.

The choral 'Ode to Joy' becomes the European Union's anthem in 1985.
moments.takeaway: Innovation within a form can also redefine its boundaries.

moments.title: Marx's Lehre
moments.body: Adolph Bernhard Marx's treatise codifies sonata form as a teaching tool. Schools have used variants of his scheme ever since.
moments.takeaway: Pedagogical clarity can flatten a more varied compositional practice.

now.title: Form analysis today
now.body: Theorists (Hepokoski and Darcy, 'Elements of Sonata Theory', 2006) propose more nuanced descriptions of Classical-era practice. Music analysis software supports automated form detection.
now.open_questions: How well do schemas derived from the Classical period describe non-Western music? What new forms emerge in algorithmic composition?

items.reflection: Listening through a form that was named only after it was composed is a small act of historical imagination.

moments.title: Phonograph invented
moments.body:
Edison's tinfoil cylinder recorder reproduces sound for the first time.

The technology will reshape both the music industry and how musical performance is studied.
moments.takeaway: Sound preservation began as a side-project in a research laboratory.

moments.title: Long-playing record
moments.body:
Peter Goldmark's 33 1/3 rpm vinyl LP holds about 22 minutes per side.

Longer forms (symphonies, jazz suites) are now sellable as complete works.
moments.takeaway: Media formats constrain and enable musical structures.

moments.title: Spotify launches
moments.body:
The streaming service launches in Europe, reaching the US in 2011.

The rise of streaming reorganises industry revenue around per-stream royalties.
moments.takeaway: Distribution technology continues to reshape musical economics.

now.title: Recorded music today
now.body: Recorded music revenues are mostly streaming. Cassette and vinyl re-emerged as smaller markets in the late 2010s. AI-generated music raises new attribution questions.
now.open_questions: What rights frameworks suit AI training on copyrighted recordings? How will live performance economics evolve?

items.reflection: Music's relationship to recording technology has been continuously renegotiated for nearly 150 years.

moments.title: Jazz emerges in New Orleans
moments.body: African American musicians draw on blues, ragtime, marching band, opera and church traditions to develop new improvisatory practices.
moments.takeaway: Jazz arose at the intersection of multiple traditions in a multilingual port city.

moments.title: First jazz recording
moments.body: A white New Orleans group makes the first commercially released jazz record before any African American jazz band.
moments.takeaway: Industry structures shaped whose innovations reached recorded history first.

moments.title: Kind of Blue
moments.body: Davis's modal jazz album becomes one of the best-selling jazz records of all time, shifting harmonic practice away from chord-change-driven improvisation.
moments.takeaway: A single album can redirect a tradition's harmonic language.

now.title: Jazz today
now.body: Jazz exists in conservatory programmes, festival circuits and ongoing creative experiment. Hip-hop, funk and electronic genres draw on its harmonic vocabulary.
now.open_questions: How are improvisational practices being reshaped by digital tools and global collaboration?

items.reflection: Recovering the history of who created jazz, and who got credit, is itself an active scholarly and curatorial project.

moments.title: Symphonia composed
moments.body: Hildegard compiles dozens of liturgical songs combining wide leaps and ecstatic melismas, unusual for plainchant of the period.
moments.takeaway: Medieval music history includes major women composers.

moments.title: Ordo Virtutum
moments.body: Hildegard composes a sung morality play, perhaps the earliest extant.
moments.takeaway: Music drama has a longer pre-operatic history than usually taught.

moments.title: Hildegard declared Doctor of the Church
moments.body: Hildegard is named one of only four women Doctors of the Catholic Church.
moments.takeaway: Twelfth-century music can return to the centre of contemporary culture.

now.title: Early music today
now.body: Hildegard's chants chart on classical streaming services. Period-instrument groups revive medieval performance practice.
now.open_questions: How should we hear medieval music designed for ritual when streamed on phones?

items.reflection: Hildegard was a polymath who wrote music as one part of her vision of the cosmos.

moments.title: Leonin's Magnus liber
moments.body: Leonin compiles a 'Great Book' of two-voice organum for the Paris liturgy.
moments.takeaway: Western polyphony has a documented origin in 12th-century Paris.

moments.title: Perotin's four-voice organum
moments.body: Perotin expands organum to four voices in works like 'Viderunt omnes'.
moments.takeaway: Polyphonic ambition grew with the Gothic cathedral that housed it.

moments.title: Franconian notation
moments.body: Franco's treatise codifies rhythmic notation, making complex polyphony transmissible.
moments.takeaway: Notation systems enable musical complexity.

now.title: Notre Dame school now
now.body: Ensembles like Anonymous 4 and the Hilliard Ensemble have made medieval polyphony available to wide audiences.
now.open_questions: How much of medieval music's performance practice is irrecoverable?

items.reflection: Notre Dame's polyphony was as architectural as its arches.

moments.title: Josquin dies
moments.body: Josquin des Prez is the most printed composer of the early 16th century.
moments.takeaway: Music printing made some Renaissance composers internationally famous.

moments.title: Missa Papae Marcelli
moments.body: Palestrina's mass is later mythologised as saving polyphony from Council of Trent censure.
moments.takeaway: Music history often runs on stories that may not be quite true.

moments.title: William Byrd's Gradualia
moments.body: Byrd composes for the proscribed Catholic liturgy in a Protestant England.
moments.takeaway: Major Renaissance music was produced under religious constraint.

now.title: Renaissance music today
now.body: Specialist choirs (The Sixteen, Stile Antico) sustain Renaissance polyphony. New editions continue to emerge.
now.open_questions: Whose music from this period have we lost or overlooked?

items.reflection: Renaissance polyphony was both deeply religious and a virtuosic craft.

moments.title: Orfeo premiered
moments.body: Orfeo, performed at the Gonzaga court, is the earliest opera still in the regular repertoire.
moments.takeaway: Opera began as a court entertainment for a small audience.

moments.title: First public opera house
moments.body: Venice opens the first paid-ticket opera house, beginning opera's commercial era.
moments.takeaway: Opera transitioned from court to market within a generation.

moments.title: L'incoronazione di Poppea
moments.body: Monteverdi's last opera dramatises Roman imperial intrigue with extraordinary harmonic invention.
moments.takeaway: An aged composer reinvented a young art form.

now.title: Opera today
now.body: Opera houses face funding pressure and audience renewal questions. Streaming and cinema relays expand reach.
now.open_questions: How does an art form built for theatres adapt to screens?

items.reflection: Opera has been declared dying since the 1700s and remains stubbornly alive.

moments.title: Vivaldi at the Pieta
moments.body: Vivaldi takes a teaching post at the Ospedale della Pieta, a girls' orphanage with a renowned music programme.
moments.takeaway: Baroque institutions trained women musicians at the highest levels.

moments.title: Four Seasons published
moments.body: The four concertos are published with sonnets describing each season, an early example of programmatic music.
moments.takeaway: Music was paired with explanatory text long before liner notes.

moments.title: Vivaldi revival
moments.body: Vivaldi's music is largely forgotten until the 20th century, when manuscript discoveries trigger a major rediscovery.
moments.takeaway: Even the most popular Baroque composer was a 20th-century rediscovery.

now.title: Baroque now
now.body: Period-instrument performance has reshaped how Vivaldi is heard. The Four Seasons is now among the most performed works in classical music.
now.open_questions: What other Baroque composers are still awaiting rediscovery?

items.reflection: Music's history depends partly on what is in someone's attic.

moments.title: Brandenburg Concertos
moments.body: Bach sends six concerti to the Margrave of Brandenburg; the dedication letter survives.
moments.takeaway: Speculative job applications produced foundational repertoire.

moments.title: St Matthew Passion
moments.body: Bach composes the Passion for Good Friday at the Thomaskirche. It is largely forgotten until Mendelssohn revives it in 1829.
moments.takeaway: Even master works can sleep for a century.

moments.title: Bach dies in Leipzig
moments.body: Bach dies after eye surgery, leaving the Art of Fugue unfinished. His sons promote his memory.
moments.takeaway: Posthumous reputations depend on family advocacy.

now.title: Bach today
now.body: Bach is now central to global music education. Glenn Gould's 1955 Goldberg Variations transformed the listening of his music.
now.open_questions: What in Bach's vast catalogue is still under-performed?

items.reflection: Bach was famous in his lifetime as an organist, not as a composer.

moments.title: Rinaldo in London
moments.body: Handel's Italian opera in London marks his arrival on the English scene.
moments.takeaway: Composers crossed borders for commercial opportunity.

moments.title: Messiah composed in 24 days
moments.body: Handel composes Messiah at speed; it premieres in Dublin in April 1742.
moments.takeaway: Iconic works were sometimes composed under intense deadline.

moments.title: Handel dies
moments.body: Handel is buried in Westminster Abbey. Messiah has been performed at Easter and Christmas continuously since.
moments.takeaway: Some pieces are inseparable from a national calendar.

now.title: Choral society tradition
now.body: Messiah singalongs persist worldwide. Handel's operas, neglected for centuries, are now a staple of period-instrument festivals.
now.open_questions: What makes some works become annual rituals?

items.reflection: Handel's Hallelujah Chorus may be the most-sung work in Western music.

moments.title: Haydn at Esterhazy
moments.body: Haydn takes a court post that will last 30 years, with an in-house orchestra to experiment with daily.
moments.takeaway: Court patronage funded sustained creative experiment.

moments.title: London symphonies
moments.body: Haydn composes 12 symphonies for Salomon's London concerts, including the 'Surprise', 'Military' and 'London'.
moments.takeaway: The market replaced the court for the late Classical symphony.

moments.title: Creation premiered
moments.body: Haydn's oratorio depicts the world's creation, including a famously dissonant 'Chaos' opening.
moments.takeaway: Religious music could be cosmically curious.

now.title: Haydn today
now.body: Haydn's 104 symphonies are increasingly recorded as complete cycles. His string quartets remain pedagogical core.
now.open_questions: How do we listen to a composer with such a vast catalogue?

items.reflection: Haydn invented the symphony as we know it, one piece at a time.

moments.title: Grand Tour
moments.body: Leopold Mozart takes his children Wolfgang (7) and Nannerl on a three-year tour of European courts.
moments.takeaway: Mozart's career was launched by his father's promotional strategy.

moments.title: Le nozze di Figaro
moments.body: Mozart and Da Ponte adapt Beaumarchais's politically charged comedy.
moments.takeaway: Late 18th-century opera engaged contemporary politics.

moments.title: Mozart dies
moments.body: Mozart dies at 35, leaving the Requiem unfinished. The myth of poisoning is later exploded.
moments.takeaway: Romantic biographies often mythologise Classical composers.

now.title: Mozart now
now.body: Mozart's complete works are available free online (NMA). His operas are foundational to international repertoire.
now.open_questions: How do we square Mozart's biography with the music?

items.reflection: Mozart's catalogue at 35 is larger than many composers' at 80.

moments.title: Heiligenstadt Testament
moments.body: Beethoven writes a letter contemplating suicide as he confronts deafness. He chooses to keep composing.
moments.takeaway: Disability is part of musical biography.

moments.title: Eroica premiered
moments.body: The Third Symphony nearly doubles the length of a typical Haydn symphony and redefines what symphonic music can do.
moments.takeaway: Beethoven enlarged the scale of orchestral thought.

moments.title: Beethoven's funeral
moments.body: 20,000 mourners attend. Schubert is a torchbearer; Schubert dies a year later and is buried nearby.
moments.takeaway: Composer reputations could approach civic event.

now.title: Beethoven now
now.body: His Ninth is the EU anthem; his Fifth Symphony's four notes are global musical shorthand. Disability scholarship reframes his late style.
now.open_questions: How should we understand the late string quartets?

items.reflection: Beethoven made the symphony into something that could not be ignored.

moments.title: Gretchen am Spinnrade
moments.body: Schubert composes his first masterpiece Lied at 17, setting Goethe.
moments.takeaway: The German Lied became a major art form in a teenager's hands.

moments.title: Winterreise
moments.body: Schubert's 24-song cycle on Wilhelm Muller's poems explores wandering, loss and snow.
moments.takeaway: Romantic song cycles told extended emotional narratives.

moments.title: Schubert dies
moments.body: Schubert dies at 31. Most of his 600 songs were unknown outside friendly circles until later publication.
moments.takeaway: Posthumous publication shaped what we now consider Schubert's canon.

now.title: Lieder today
now.body: Winterreise remains a Liederabend touchstone, with cross-genre performances by Ian Bostridge and others.
now.open_questions: How does intimate song survive in an arena age?

items.reflection: Schubert wrote songs the way many composers later wrote operas.

moments.title: Symphonie fantastique
moments.body: Berlioz's autobiographical symphony embeds an opium dream and an idee fixe across five movements.
moments.takeaway: Romantic music made composers' inner lives the subject.

moments.title: Chopin in Paris
moments.body: Chopin settles in Paris after the November Uprising in Poland. He never returns home.
moments.takeaway: Exile reshaped 19th-century musical geography.

moments.title: Chopin dies
moments.body: Chopin dies at 39 of tuberculosis. His heart is sent back to Warsaw.
moments.takeaway: Romantic biographies merged music, nationhood and the body.

now.title: Romantic piano now
now.body: Chopin competitions in Warsaw remain among the most prestigious. Berlioz is studied as a key figure in orchestration history.
now.open_questions: How should we hear music written for instruments that have changed?

items.reflection: Romanticism made the piano a personal voice for millions.

moments.title: Wagner exiled
moments.body: After participating in the May Uprising, Wagner is exiled to Switzerland. He begins planning the Ring there.
moments.takeaway: Political dissent shaped operatic ambition.

moments.title: Der Ring des Nibelungen
moments.body: Wagner completes the four-opera Ring Cycle, premiered at his purpose-built Festspielhaus.
moments.takeaway: A composer built his own theatre to stage his work.

moments.title: Wagner dies
moments.body: Wagner's legacy includes both the leitmotif technique and his explicit anti-Semitism, weaponised by later fascists.
moments.takeaway: Music history must hold both achievement and harm.

now.title: Wagner now
now.body: Bayreuth performances are critical and controversial events. Israeli orchestras have only recently begun performing Wagner.
now.open_questions: How do we play music whose composer's politics we reject?

items.reflection: Wagner asks more from his audience than almost any other Western composer.

moments.title: Brahms's First Symphony
moments.body: Brahms releases his First Symphony after a 20-year struggle, sometimes called 'Beethoven's Tenth'.
moments.takeaway: Composing in someone else's shadow can be a 20-year project.

moments.title: Swan Lake
moments.body: Tchaikovsky's first ballet flops on premiere but later becomes a global standard.
moments.takeaway: Initial reception can be wildly different from posterity.

moments.title: Tchaikovsky dies
moments.body: Tchaikovsky dies days after conducting the premiere of his Sixth Symphony 'Pathetique'. Causes remain debated.
moments.takeaway: Biographical mysteries persist about even the most studied composers.

now.title: Late Romanticism
now.body: Brahms's symphonies remain orchestral cornerstones. Tchaikovsky's ballets dominate Christmas season programming.
now.open_questions: How are queer readings of 19th-century composers shaping the canon?

items.reflection: The 19th-century symphony orchestra is essentially the orchestra we still use.

moments.title: Mahler's nine symphonies
moments.body: Mahler expands the symphony to over 90 minutes, with vocal soloists, choirs and offstage bands.
moments.takeaway: The late Romantic symphony reached unprecedented scale.

moments.title: Director of the Vienna Court Opera
moments.body: Mahler raises performance standards in Vienna but faces antisemitic abuse from the press.
moments.takeaway: Antisemitism shaped the careers of Jewish musicians in central Europe.

moments.title: Mahler dies
moments.body: Mahler dies leaving the Tenth Symphony incomplete. Later 'performing versions' (Cooke, 1964) make it accessible.
moments.takeaway: Unfinished works can have multiple lives.

now.title: Mahler today
now.body: His symphonies were neglected for decades and revived by Leonard Bernstein from the 1960s onwards.
now.open_questions: What is the future of long-form symphonic music?

items.reflection: Mahler thought a symphony should contain a world. His do.

moments.title: Prelude a l'apres-midi d'un faune
moments.body: Pierre Boulez later called this 10-minute work the moment modern music begins.
moments.takeaway: Modernist music had a soft, fluid beginning.

moments.title: La Mer
moments.body: Debussy's three symphonic sketches of the sea, with their Hokusai-derived cover, draw on non-Western influences.
moments.takeaway: Modernism absorbed visual and global culture.

moments.title: Debussy dies
moments.body: Debussy dies during World War I. His tonal experiments shape 20th-century jazz harmony.
moments.takeaway: Impressionism in music influenced popular as much as classical idioms.

now.title: French modernism now
now.body: Boulez and Pierre-Laurent Aimard have championed French modernist recordings. Debussy's harmony now underpins much film scoring.
now.open_questions: How much do current 'pretty' harmonies owe to Debussy?

items.reflection: Music could move without obvious cadences. Debussy proved it.

moments.title: Rite of Spring premiere
moments.who: Igor Stravinsky and Vaslav Nijinsky, Paris
moments.body: The premiere at the Theatre des Champs-Elysees provokes a famous riot, with audience members fighting in the aisles.
moments.takeaway: Modernism's most cited scandal was as much about choreography as score.

moments.title: Schoenberg's twelve-tone method
moments.body: Schoenberg articulates serialism, organising music around 12 equal pitch classes.
moments.takeaway: Composers tried to escape tonality through formal systems.

moments.title: Stravinsky dies
moments.body: Stravinsky's career spans late Romantic, neoclassical and serial phases.
moments.takeaway: Major composers can change idiom every decade.

now.title: Modernism in repertoire
now.body: The Rite is now one of the most-performed 20th-century works. Schoenberg remains less popular but central to teaching.
now.open_questions: What makes one piece of modernism catch on and another not?

items.reflection: Audience riots over music are rare and revealing.

moments.body: Cage's piece instructs a pianist not to play for 4 minutes 33 seconds. Ambient sounds are the work.
moments.takeaway: Experimental music can put a frame around what is already there.

moments.title: It's Gonna Rain
moments.body: Reich's tape piece phases two identical loops slightly out of sync, founding minimalist process music.
moments.takeaway: Tape technology shaped new composition strategies.

moments.title: Einstein on the Beach
moments.body: Glass's five-hour opera, with no intermission, redefines what an opera could be.
moments.takeaway: Minimalism transformed not just music but stage time.

now.title: Minimalism today
now.body: Minimalist gestures pervade film scores, ambient music and pop production.
now.open_questions: Is contemporary 'lo-fi' or 'chill' music minimalism in another guise?

items.reflection: Strip music down far enough and you discover new possibilities.

moments.title: Johnson records
moments.who: Robert Johnson, San Antonio and Dallas
moments.body: Johnson records 29 songs in two sessions for ARC, including 'Cross Road Blues'.
moments.takeaway: Some of the most influential 20th-century music was captured in days.

moments.title: Johnson dies
moments.body: Johnson dies at 27, possibly poisoned. The crossroads myth grows around his short life.
moments.takeaway: Blues mythology has shaped how we hear the music.

moments.title: King of the Delta Blues Singers
moments.body: The reissue introduces Johnson to a new generation, including the Rolling Stones, Eric Clapton and Bob Dylan.
moments.takeaway: Rock and roll's foundations include records most listeners never heard at first issue.

now.title: Blues lineage
now.body: Hill Country blues, Chicago blues and contemporary acts (Christone 'Kingfish' Ingram) sustain the tradition.
now.open_questions: Who owns and who benefits from the blues legacy now?

items.reflection: Almost everything rock and roll became starts in two recording sessions in Texas.

moments.title: Grand Ole Opry begins
moments.body: The barn-dance broadcast turns Nashville into the country music capital.
moments.takeaway: Radio shaped which cities became music industries.

moments.title: Lovesick Blues
moments.body: Williams's recording becomes a country standard and a tour staple. His honky-tonk sound dominates the era.
moments.takeaway: Country music had its own gravitational centre.

moments.title: Williams dies
moments.body: Williams dies in the back of his Cadillac at 29, en route to a concert.
moments.takeaway: Country's tragic biographies became part of its mythology.

now.title: Country today
now.body: Country has become commercially dominant in the US; debates about its identity (genre fluidity, race) continue.
now.open_questions: Who counts as 'country' in the streaming era?

items.reflection: Country music began as folk and became commercial without ever quite leaving the porch.

moments.title: Elvis on Ed Sullivan
moments.body: Elvis's Ed Sullivan appearances reach over 60 million viewers, scandalising parents and launching rock and roll.
moments.takeaway: Television shaped rock's mass arrival.

moments.title: Beatles in America
moments.body: The Beatles' Ed Sullivan appearance draws 73 million viewers, launching the British Invasion.
moments.takeaway: Pop music globalised faster than other arts.

moments.title: Dylan goes electric
moments.body: Dylan's electric set provokes booing from folk purists.
moments.takeaway: Genre boundaries are defended by audiences.

now.title: Rock's afterlife
now.body: The Beatles' catalogue is now a major streaming asset. AI-restored 'final' Beatles songs (2023) blur authorship.
now.open_questions: What does rock mean to listeners born after 2000?

items.reflection: Rock and roll was a youth phenomenon that grew old.

moments.title: Hendrix at Woodstock
moments.body: Hendrix's distorted Star-Spangled Banner at dawn becomes a defining performance.
moments.takeaway: Rock's most political moments are often instrumental.

moments.title: Stairway to Heaven
moments.body: Released on Led Zeppelin IV, the song becomes the most-requested track on FM radio.
moments.takeaway: Rock could write epic narrative without lyrics or operas.

moments.title: Sex Pistols on Bill Grundy
moments.body: A profanity-laden TV interview launches punk into the British mainstream.
moments.takeaway: Punk used television scandal as much as Elvis had.

now.title: Rock now
now.body: Rock's market share has fallen; legacy acts dominate touring revenue. Indie rock thrives in fragmented niches.
now.open_questions: Will guitar bands again dominate pop charts?

items.reflection: Rock keeps not dying.

moments.title: DJ Kool Herc's party
moments.who: Cindy Campbell and Clive Campbell, Bronx
moments.body: An 11 August birthday party at 1520 Sedgwick Avenue is later identified as hip-hop's founding event.
moments.takeaway: Cultural histories can be dated to a single block party.

moments.title: Rapper's Delight
moments.body: The 14-minute single becomes the first commercially successful hip-hop record.
moments.takeaway: Underground innovations reach mass audiences through small labels.

moments.title: Public Enemy and N.W.A albums
moments.body: It Takes a Nation of Millions to Hold Us Back and Straight Outta Compton politicise hip-hop nationally.
moments.takeaway: Hip-hop developed multiple regional voices in parallel.

now.title: Hip-hop today
now.body: Hip-hop is the most-streamed genre in the US (RIAA 2017 onwards). It has globalised through K-pop, Afrobeats and UK drill.
now.open_questions: How do regional hip-hops change the global sound?

items.reflection: What started in the Bronx is now the lingua franca of pop.

moments.title: Autobahn
moments.body: Kraftwerk's 22-minute title track and edited single bring synthesiser music to mass audiences.
moments.takeaway: Electronic music had its own pop breakthrough.

moments.title: Acid house in Manchester
moments.body: Detroit techno and Chicago house transform via Manchester clubs into UK rave culture.
moments.takeaway: Electronic music's geography is fluid and global.

moments.title: Daft Punk's Discovery
moments.body: The album marries house with sampled disco, shaping pop production for two decades.
moments.takeaway: Electronic music keeps re-entering the mainstream in new disguises.

now.title: Electronic now
now.body: Producers like SOPHIE and Arca reshape pop sound design. AI music tools democratise composition.
now.open_questions: Is there a recognisable 'electronic' anymore when everything is electronic?

items.reflection: Synthesisers stopped being the future and became the default.

moments.title: Thriller
moments.body: Thriller is the bestselling album of all time, with the title video reshaping pop video as a form.
moments.takeaway: Music and video became inseparable in the 1980s.

moments.title: Like a Virgin
moments.body: Madonna's image and performance reshape what a female pop star looks and sounds like.
moments.takeaway: Pop turned image into instrument.

moments.title: Jackson dies
moments.body: Jackson's death prompts global mourning and renewed debate over abuse allegations.
moments.takeaway: Pop biographies must hold celebration and harm together.

now.title: Pop now
now.body: Taylor Swift and BTS run touring economies on a national scale. Spotify and TikTok shape what gets heard.
now.open_questions: Who shapes pop now, artists or algorithms?

items.reflection: Pop has been declared throwaway and survived every generation that said so.

moments.title: Cristofori's pianoforte
moments.body: Cristofori invents a keyboard instrument with hammers that can be played loud or soft.
moments.takeaway: The most popular Western instrument was invented by a single craftsman.

moments.title: Saxophone patented
moments.body: Sax's hybrid woodwind-brass instrument is intended for military bands and becomes essential to jazz.
moments.takeaway: Instruments designed for one purpose can be hijacked by another tradition.

moments.title: Electric guitar
moments.body: The Rickenbacker 'Frying Pan' is the first commercially produced electric guitar.
moments.takeaway: Electrification reshaped what string instruments could do.

now.title: Instruments now
now.body: Software instruments and modelling let any sound become a controller. The piano remains the most learned instrument worldwide.
now.open_questions: What is an 'instrument' when everything can be a control surface?

items.reflection: Instrument design is the most enduring craft in music history.

moments.title: Guido d'Arezzo's staff
moments.body: Guido develops the four-line staff and a solmisation system using syllables (ut, re, mi...) drawn from a hymn.
moments.takeaway: Notation made music transmissible across distance and time.

moments.title: Petrucci prints music
moments.body: Petrucci publishes the first polyphonic music book printed with movable type.
moments.takeaway: Music printing turned local repertoire into international.

moments.title: MusicXML released
moments.body: MusicXML becomes the de facto interchange format for digital scores.
moments.takeaway: Each era's notation reflects its dominant technology.

now.title: Notation today
now.body: MuseScore, Dorico and Sibelius let amateurs typeset music. Streaming services now display lyrics syncing with playback.
now.open_questions: Will notation survive as listeners increasingly bypass scores?

items.reflection: Without notation, most of the world's classical traditions would not be teachable.

moments.title: Ravi Shankar at Monterey
moments.body: Shankar's sitar performance brings Hindustani classical music to a mass Western audience.
moments.takeaway: Festivals globalised non-Western traditions.

moments.title: Steve Reich studies Ghanaian drumming
moments.body: Reich studies at the University of Ghana, feeding African polyrhythm into American minimalism.
moments.takeaway: Cross-cultural study shaped 20th-century composition.

moments.title: Graceland
moments.body: Simon's album with Ladysmith Black Mambazo and other South African musicians faces anti-apartheid boycott debate.
moments.takeaway: World music collaborations carry political weight.

now.title: World music now
now.body: Streaming flattens listening geography; K-pop and Afrobeats top global charts.
now.open_questions: What does 'world music' mean when the global is everywhere?

items.reflection: Most of the world's music history is not Western.

moments.title: King Kong score
moments.body: Steiner's symphonic score sets the template for Golden Age Hollywood music.
moments.takeaway: Cinema absorbed Wagnerian leitmotif technique.

moments.title: Star Wars
moments.body: Williams's score, recorded by the LSO, revives the symphonic blockbuster.
moments.takeaway: Film music revived orchestral writing for mass audiences.

moments.title: Hildur Gudnadottir wins Oscar
moments.body: Gudnadottir becomes only the third woman to win an original score Oscar.
moments.takeaway: Major film scoring is still mostly male-dominated.

now.title: Film music today
now.body: TV scoring (Cuarron, Reznor) blurs cinema and television soundtracks. Video game music reaches concert hall.
now.open_questions: What is the next platform that will reshape scoring?

items.reflection: Most listeners hear more orchestral music in cinemas than in concert halls.

moments.title: Clara Schumann's last public composition
moments.body: Clara Schumann effectively stops composing at 34, after Robert's breakdown. Her existing works grow in reputation.
moments.takeaway: Composing careers are interrupted by life circumstances.

moments.title: March of the Women
moments.body: Smyth's suffragette anthem is sung outside Holloway Prison while she conducts with a toothbrush.
moments.takeaway: Composition could be openly political.

moments.title: Florence Price retrospective
moments.body: Lost Price scores rediscovered in 2009 enter major orchestral programming.
moments.takeaway: Recovery work continues to reshape canon.

now.title: Women composers now
now.body: Conductors like Marin Alsop and composer-in-residence programmes are slowly rebalancing programmes.
now.open_questions: How long does it take to recover a century's worth of overlooked work?

items.reflection: The canon is a curating choice, not a natural fact.

moments.title: West Side Story
moments.body: The young Sondheim writes lyrics for Bernstein's score. The musical refashions Romeo and Juliet for New York gangs.
moments.takeaway: Major theatre work often comes from collaborations across generations.

moments.title: Company
moments.body: Company introduces the 'concept musical', built around themes rather than plot.
moments.takeaway: Musical theatre kept reinventing its own form.

moments.title: Hamilton
moments.body: Miranda's hip-hop musical retells Alexander Hamilton's life with a Black and brown cast.
moments.takeaway: Musical theatre absorbs the dominant popular idiom of its day.

now.title: Musical theatre today
now.body: Streaming captures of stage productions (Hamilton on Disney+) reach mass audiences. West End and Broadway recover from pandemic shutdowns.
now.open_questions: What musical genre does theatre adopt next?

items.reflection: Musicals are pop music for the stage and theatre for pop audiences.
